title: Summary Ranges
statement_short: Given a sorted unique integer array nums, return the smallest sorted list of ranges that cover all the numbers in the array exactly. Each range [a,b] should be output as "a->b" if a != b, or "a" if a == b.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 20, -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1, all values of nums are unique, nums is sorted in ascending order
hint: Small length limit (<= 20) allows a single-pass linear scan with start-end pointers.
keywords: nums is sorted in ascending order
why_not: Right: Two Pointers (or single-pass boundary pointers) tracks contiguous range start and end indices in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Intervals: Interval merging algorithms merge overlapping ranges, whereas this input consists of sorted single numbers forming contiguous increments. Not Sliding Window: Sliding window techniques compute subsegment totals/conditions rather than partitioning contiguous consecutive numbers. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash sets ignore sorted sequence order, incurring unnecessary memory.
